bull.b: Arm’s licensing and royalty model lets multiple customers build products on the same architecture while generating recurring per-unit revenue as chips ship. Broad exposure across mobile, automotive, embedded, infrastructure and other markets supports scalable monetization and reduces dependence on a single end market.

Rapid data-center royalty growth and stronger-than-expected AGI CPU demand indicate Arm is gaining relevance in energy-efficient AI infrastructure. Adoption by major cloud and technology partners can deepen the ecosystem and create durable royalty opportunities as AI workloads expand across data centers and edge devices.

Very high gross margins, strong operating profitability, substantial free cash flow and minimal leverage provide Arm with financial flexibility. This profile supports continued investment in research, tools and ecosystem development while reducing balance-sheet pressure during periods of market or product transition.

bear.b: Smartphones remain an important royalty market, so weaker handset demand and memory-driven bill-of-material pressure can reduce chip volumes and delay royalty growth. Management’s low-teens near-term royalty outlook shows that this established business is currently growing more slowly than earlier expectations.

Demand above the initial AGI CPU target may not translate promptly into revenue because production depends on securing several constrained inputs and manufacturing capacities. These bottlenecks can delay customer deployments, limit near-term silicon volumes and defer the commercial benefit of the opportunity.

The AGI CPU’s initial gross-margin profile is materially below Arm’s traditional IP economics, creating dilution risk as the company expands into production silicon. Until scale, product mix and execution improve margins toward the long-term target, growth in this business may deliver less incremental profit.
